```{r development, include=FALSE}
library(testthat)
```

Repeated, optionally stratified k-fold cross-validation, implemented with base R and `data.table`. `split_cv()` works on a list of tables, `nest_cv()` on a nested table such as the output of `w2l_nest()`. Folds are returned as row indices and, optionally, as training / validation subsets (`data.table` or `data.frame`).

# Cross-validation for a list of tables: `split_cv()`
    
```{r function-split_cv}
#' Apply V-Fold Cross-Validation to a List of Datasets
#'
#' @description
#' `split_cv` creates (optionally repeated and stratified) v-fold
#' cross-validation splits for every dataset in a list. It is implemented
#' with base R and `data.table` only and returns, per dataset, a
#' `data.table` of fold identifiers, row indices and (optionally) the
#' training / validation subsets.
#'
#' @param data     A `list` whose every element is a `data.frame` or
#'   `data.table`. Must be non-empty. A single `data.frame` is not accepted
#'   (wrap it in `list()`).
#' @param v        Number of folds. A single integer >= 2. Default `10`.
#' @param repeats  Number of repeats. A single integer >= 1. Default `1`.
#' @param strata   `NULL` (default) or a single column name present in
#'   **every** dataset. Rows are shuffled within each stratum so that every
#'   fold receives a proportional share of each stratum.
#' @param breaks   Number of quantile bins used when `strata` is numeric with
#'   more than `breaks` distinct values. Default `4`.
#' @param pool     Strata holding less than this proportion of the rows are
#'   merged with the next-smallest stratum. A number in `[0, 0.5)`.
#'   Default `0.1`.
#' @param seed     `NULL` (default) or a single number for reproducible folds.
#'   The caller's random-number stream is restored on exit.
#' @param materialize Logical. If `TRUE` (default), `train` / `validate`
#'   list-columns holding the subsets are added. `FALSE` keeps only the row
#'   indices, which needs far less memory for large data.
#' @param out_type Class of the `train` / `validate` subsets: `"dt"`
#'   (`data.table`, default) or `"df"` (plain `data.frame`, e.g. for
#'   'ASReml-R' or other modelling functions that expect a `data.frame`).
#'   Factor levels are kept in full in every subset. Only used when
#'   `materialize = TRUE`; the returned fold table itself is always a
#'   `data.table`.
#'
#' @details
#' Fold sizes differ by at most one row. With stratification, rows are
#' shuffled within strata, the strata are laid out one after another and fold
#' labels are dealt out cyclically, so each stratum is spread evenly across
#' folds. The stratification rules (`breaks`, `pool`) follow the same idea
#' as `rsample::vfold_cv()`, but the random fold assignments are not
#' identical to rsample's.
#'
#' Training and validation subsets can always be rebuilt from the indices:
#' `data[[1]][res[[1]]$train_idx[[k]], ]`.
#'
#' For mixed-model cross-validation (e.g. genomic prediction with
#' 'ASReml-R') a common alternative to subsetting is masking: keep all
#' records, set the phenotypes of `validate_idx` to `NA`, fit the model on
#' the full data and correlate the predicted breeding values of the masked
#' individuals with their observations. `materialize = FALSE` is enough for
#' this, since only the indices are needed.
#'
#' @return A `list` of `data.table` objects (one per input dataset, names of
#'   `data` preserved), each with one row per fold and the columns:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item `id`           — fold label (`Fold1`, ...), or repeat label
#'         (`Repeat1`, ...) when `repeats > 1`.
#'   \item `id2`          — fold label, only when `repeats > 1`.
#'   \item `train_idx`    — list-column of training row indices.
#'   \item `validate_idx` — list-column of validation row indices.
#'   \item `train`, `validate` — list-columns of subsets, `data.table` or
#'         `data.frame` according to `out_type` (only when
#'         `materialize = TRUE`).
#' }
#'
#' @seealso [nest_cv()] for the nested `data.table` variant.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
split_cv <- function(data,
                     v           = 10L,
                     repeats     = 1L,
                     strata      = NULL,
                     breaks      = 4L,
                     pool        = 0.1,
                     seed        = NULL,
                     materialize = TRUE,
                     out_type    = "dt") {

  # -- 1. Input validation (once, before the loop) -----------------------------
  # A data.frame is also a list, so it must be rejected explicitly; otherwise
  # its columns would be treated as datasets.
  if (!is.list(data) || is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a list of data.frames/data.tables. ",
         "To use a single data.frame, wrap it in list(). Received: ",
         paste(class(data), collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)
  if (length(data) == 0L)
    stop("`data` must not be empty.", call. = FALSE)
  v       <- .check_count(v, "v", 2L)
  repeats <- .check_count(repeats, "repeats", 1L)
  breaks  <- .check_count(breaks, "breaks", 2L)
  if (!is.numeric(pool) || length(pool) != 1L || is.na(pool) || pool < 0 || pool >= 0.5)
    stop("`pool` must be a single number in [0, 0.5).", call. = FALSE)
  .check_flag(materialize, "materialize")
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  is_valid <- vapply(data, is.data.frame, logical(1L))
  if (!all(is_valid)) {
    bad_idx <- which(!is_valid)
    stop("All elements of `data` must be data.frames or data.tables.\n",
         "  Invalid element(s) at index: ", paste(bad_idx, collapse = ", "),
         "\n  Types received: ",
         paste(vapply(data[bad_idx], function(x) class(x)[1L], character(1L)),
               collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  too_small <- vapply(data, nrow, integer(1L)) < v
  if (any(too_small))
    stop("Dataset(s) at index ", paste(which(too_small), collapse = ", "),
         " have fewer rows than `v` (", v, ").", call. = FALSE)

  if (!is.null(strata)) {
    if (!is.character(strata) || length(strata) != 1L || is.na(strata))
      stop("`strata` must be a single character string (column name).", call. = FALSE)
    strata_missing <- vapply(data, function(df) !strata %in% names(df), logical(1L))
    if (any(strata_missing)) {
      missing_idx <- which(strata_missing)
      stop("The `strata` column '", strata,
           "' is absent from dataset(s) at index: ",
           paste(missing_idx, collapse = ", "),
           if (!is.null(names(data)))
             paste0(" (name(s): '", paste(names(data)[missing_idx],
                                          collapse = "', '"), "')"),
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }

  # -- 2. Fold assignment for every dataset -------------------------------------
  run <- function() {
    out <- lapply(data, function(x) {
      x <- if (data.table::is.data.table(x)) x else data.table::as.data.table(x)
      .vfold_table(x, v = v, repeats = repeats, strata = strata,
                   breaks = breaks, pool = pool, materialize = materialize,
                   out_type = out_type)
    })
    names(out) <- names(data)
    out
  }
  # A non-NULL seed makes the folds reproducible without disturbing the
  # caller's RNG stream.
  .with_seed(seed, run())
}
```
  
```{r example-split_cv}
# Prepare example data: Convert first 3 columns of iris dataset to long format and split
dt_split <- w2l_split(data = iris, cols = 1:3)
# dt_split is now a list containing 3 data tables for Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, and Petal.Length

# Example 1: Single cross-validation (no repeats)
split_cv(
  data = dt_split,      # Input list of split data
  v = 3,                # Set 3-fold cross-validation
  repeats = 1,          # Perform cross-validation once (no repeats)
  seed = 123            # Reproducible folds
)
# Returns a list where each element contains:
# - id: fold labels (Fold1, Fold2, Fold3)
# - train_idx / validate_idx: row indices of each fold
# - train / validate: training and validation subsets

# Example 2: Repeated cross-validation
split_cv(
  data = dt_split,      # Input list of split data
  v = 3,                # Set 3-fold cross-validation
  repeats = 2,          # Perform cross-validation twice
  seed = 123
)
# Returns a list where each element contains:
# - id: repeat labels (Repeat1, Repeat2)
# - id2: fold labels (Fold1, Fold2, Fold3)
# - train_idx / validate_idx, train / validate

# Example 3: Stratified CV, indices only (memory friendly)
res <- split_cv(dt_split, v = 5, strata = "Species", seed = 1,
                materialize = FALSE)
# Rebuild the training set of fold 1 of the first dataset when needed
head(dt_split[[1]][res[[1]]$train_idx[[1]], ])
```

```{r tests-split_cv}
test_that("split_cv creates complete, disjoint and balanced folds", {
  res <- split_cv(list(a = iris), v = 4, seed = 1)$a
  expect_identical(res$id, paste0("Fold", 1:4))
  v_idx <- res$validate_idx
  expect_identical(sort(unlist(v_idx)), 1:150)
  expect_true(max(lengths(v_idx)) - min(lengths(v_idx)) <= 1)
  for (k in 1:4) {
    expect_length(intersect(res$train_idx[[k]], v_idx[[k]]), 0)
    expect_identical(nrow(res$validate[[k]]), length(v_idx[[k]]))
  }
})

test_that("split_cv labels repeats and pads fold numbers", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 10, repeats = 2, seed = 1)[[1]]
  expect_identical(names(res)[1:2], c("id", "id2"))
  expect_identical(unique(res$id), c("Repeat1", "Repeat2"))
  expect_identical(res$id2[1:2], c("Fold01", "Fold02"))
})

test_that("split_cv stratifies categorical and numeric variables", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 5, strata = "Species", seed = 2)[[1]]
  counts <- vapply(res$validate, function(d) as.integer(table(d$Species)), integer(3))
  expect_true(all(counts == 10L))
  expect_silent(split_cv(list(mtcars), v = 4, strata = "mpg", breaks = 3))
})

test_that("split_cv seed is reproducible and does not disturb the RNG", {
  set.seed(9); ref <- runif(1)
  set.seed(9)
  a <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE)
  expect_identical(runif(1), ref)
  expect_identical(a, split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE))
})

test_that("split_cv out_type = 'df' returns plain data.frames with full factor levels", {
  res <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 1, out_type = "df")[[1]]
  expect_s3_class(res, "data.table")                       # fold table itself
  for (d in c(res$train, res$validate)) {
    expect_s3_class(d, "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
    expect_identical(levels(d$Species), levels(iris$Species))
  }
  ref <- iris[res$validate_idx[[1]], ]
  rownames(ref) <- NULL
  expect_equal(res$validate[[1]], ref)
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, out_type = "tibble"), "out_type")
})

test_that("split_cv out_type does not change the folds", {
  a <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 5, out_type = "dt")[[1]]
  b <- split_cv(list(iris), v = 3, seed = 5, out_type = "df")[[1]]
  expect_identical(a$validate_idx, b$validate_idx)
  expect_equal(as.data.frame(a$train[[2]]), b$train[[2]])
})

test_that("split_cv validates its input", {
  expect_error(split_cv(iris), "wrap it in list")
  expect_error(split_cv(list()), "empty")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris[1:3, ]), v = 5), "fewer rows")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), strata = "nope"), "absent")
  expect_error(split_cv(list(iris), v = 1), "`v`")
})
```

# Cross-validation inside a nested table: `nest_cv()`
    
```{r function-nest_cv}
#' Apply V-Fold Cross-Validation to Nested Data
#'
#' @description
#' `nest_cv` creates v-fold cross-validation splits for each nested data frame
#' of a nested `data.table` (e.g. the output of [w2l_nest()]) and returns one
#' row per fold, with the outer (non-nested) columns broadcast to every fold.
#' The cross-validation itself is performed by [split_cv()].
#'
#' @param data    A `data.frame` or `data.table` containing at least one nested
#'   `data.frame`/`data.table` column. A column named `data` is used if
#'   present, otherwise the first nested column.
#' @inheritParams split_cv
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with all non-nested columns of `data`, followed by
#'   the columns described in [split_cv()] (`id`, `id2`, `train_idx`,
#'   `validate_idx` and, if `materialize = TRUE`, `train` / `validate`, whose
#'   class follows `out_type`).
#'   Other nested columns are dropped (a message lists them). Non-nested
#'   columns must not use these names (an error is raised instead of
#'   creating duplicated columns).
#'
#' @seealso [split_cv()]
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
nest_cv <- function(data,
                    v           = 10L,
                    repeats     = 1L,
                    strata      = NULL,
                    breaks      = 4L,
                    pool        = 0.1,
                    seed        = NULL,
                    materialize = TRUE,
                    out_type    = "dt") {
  nest_dt <- data

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(nest_dt))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table. Received: ",
         paste(class(nest_dt), collapse = "/"), call. = FALSE)
  if (nrow(nest_dt) == 0L)
    stop("`data` must not be empty (0 rows).", call. = FALSE)

  # -- 2. Identify nested columns ----------------------------------------------
  nested_cols <- names(nest_dt)[vapply(nest_dt, function(col) {
    is.list(col) && length(col) > 0L &&
      all(vapply(col, is.data.frame, logical(1L)))
  }, logical(1L))]

  if (length(nested_cols) == 0L)
    stop("`data` contains no nested data.frame/data.table columns.\n",
         "  Column types detected: ",
         paste(names(nest_dt),
               vapply(nest_dt, function(x) class(x)[1L], character(1L)),
               sep = "=", collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  target_col <- if ("data" %in% nested_cols) "data" else nested_cols[1L]
  if (target_col != "data")
    message("[nest_cv] No nested column named 'data' found. Using '", target_col,
            "' instead.\n          Available nested columns: ",
            paste(nested_cols, collapse = ", "))
  if (length(nested_cols) > 1L)
    message("[nest_cv] Only '", target_col, "' is split; other nested column(s) ",
            "are dropped from the result: ",
            paste(setdiff(nested_cols, target_col), collapse = ", "))

  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(nest_dt)) nest_dt else data.table::as.data.table(nest_dt)
  non_nested_cols <- setdiff(names(dt), nested_cols)

  # -- 3. Delegate the CV work to split_cv() (single implementation) ----------
  cv_list <- split_cv(
    data        = dt[[target_col]],
    v           = v,
    repeats     = repeats,
    strata      = strata,
    breaks      = breaks,
    pool        = pool,
    seed        = seed,
    materialize = materialize,
    out_type    = out_type
  )

  # -- 4. Broadcast each row's metadata across its CV rows and bind ------------
  cv_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(cv_list, use.names = TRUE)
  if (length(non_nested_cols) == 0L) return(cv_dt)
  # Without this check cbind() would silently create duplicated column names
  # (e.g. a grouping column called `id`).
  .check_reserved(non_nested_cols, names(cv_dt), "nest_cv", "Grouping column(s)",
                  "these names are used for the cross-validation columns")

  n_cv <- vapply(cv_list, nrow, integer(1L))
  meta <- dt[rep(seq_len(nrow(dt)), n_cv), non_nested_cols, with = FALSE]
  cbind(meta, cv_dt)
}
```
  
```{r example-nest_cv}
# Example: Cross-validation for nested data.table demonstrations

# Setup test data
dt_nest <- w2l_nest(
  data = iris,                   # Input dataset
  cols = 1:2                     # Nest first 2 columns
)

# Example 1: Basic 2-fold cross-validation (reproducible)
nest_cv(
  data = dt_nest,                # Input nested data.table
  v = 2,                         # Number of folds (2-fold CV)
  seed = 123                     # Reproducible folds
)

# Example 2: Repeated 2-fold CV, keeping only the split objects
nest_cv(
  data = dt_nest,                # Input nested data.table
  v = 2,                         # Number of folds (2-fold CV)
  repeats = 2,                   # Number of repetitions
  seed = 123,
  materialize = FALSE            # No train/validate copies (saves memory)
)

# Example 3: data.frame subsets, ready for ASReml-R / lm() / glm()
cv_df <- nest_cv(dt_nest, v = 2, seed = 123, out_type = "df")
class(cv_df$train[[1]])        # "data.frame"

# Example 4: masking-style CV (keep all rows, hide validation phenotypes)
cv_idx <- nest_cv(dt_nest, v = 2, seed = 123, materialize = FALSE)
cv_idx[dt_nest, on = "name", full := i.data]   # attach the full nested table
masked <- as.data.frame(cv_idx$full[[1]])      # a copy: dt_nest stays intact
masked$value[cv_idx$validate_idx[[1]]] <- NA
sum(is.na(masked$value))       # validation records to be predicted
```

```{r tests-nest_cv}
test_that("nest_cv broadcasts metadata and partitions every nested table", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  res <- nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1)
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 6L * 5L)
  expect_identical(names(res)[1:3], c("name", "Species", "id"))
  one <- res[name == "Sepal.Length" & Species == "setosa"]
  expect_identical(sort(unlist(one$validate_idx)), 1:50)
  expect_equal(nrow(one$train[[1]]) + nrow(one$validate[[1]]), 50L)
})

test_that("nest_cv is reproducible and supports materialize = FALSE", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1, by = "Species")
  a <- nest_cv(nd, v = 3, seed = 7, materialize = FALSE)
  b <- nest_cv(nd, v = 3, seed = 7, materialize = FALSE)
  expect_identical(a, b)
  expect_false(any(c("train", "validate") %in% names(a)))
})

test_that("nest_cv out_type = 'df' gives data.frame subsets", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1, by = "Species")
  res <- nest_cv(nd, v = 2, seed = 1, out_type = "df")
  expect_true(all(vapply(c(res$train, res$validate),
                         function(d) identical(class(d), "data.frame"), logical(1L))))
})

test_that("masking with validate_idx leaves the nested data untouched", {
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  cv <- nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1, materialize = FALSE)
  cv[nd, on = c("name", "Species"), full := i.data]
  n_masked <- mapply(function(full, vidx) {
    d <- as.data.frame(full)
    d$value[vidx] <- NA
    sum(is.na(d$value))
  }, cv$full, cv$validate_idx)
  expect_identical(n_masked, lengths(cv$validate_idx))
  expect_false(anyNA(unlist(lapply(nd$data, `[[`, "value"))))
})

test_that("nest_cv validates its input", {
  expect_error(nest_cv(iris), "no nested")
})

test_that("nest_cv rejects grouping columns named like CV columns", {
  nd <- data.table::data.table(id = c("A", "B"),
                               data = list(data.frame(y = 1:20), data.frame(y = 1:20)))
  expect_error(nest_cv(nd, v = 5, seed = 1), "'id'")
})
```
